subject: physics
question_text: Define the intensity of the gravitational field at a point. Write its SI unit.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: The intensity of the gravitational field at a
point is the force experienced by a body of
UNIT mass placed at that point:

lines.text: E = F / m = G M / r²

steps.why: Dividing out the test mass leaves a property of the SOURCE alone, which is what makes a field useful.
common_mistakes: Defining it as the force on the source mass rather than on a unit test mass.

recall.must_convey: That it is the force on a unit mass at that point, equal to G M by r squared.

steps.label: The unit

lines.text: SI unit: N kg⁻¹ (the same as m s⁻²)

lines: It is a VECTOR, directed towards the mass that
produces the field. At the surface of the earth
steps.why: That the unit is also that of acceleration is not a coincidence: field intensity and acceleration due to gravity are the same quantity. The direction line is part of the answer, not optional: field intensity is a vector, and a definition or unit answer that drops the direction is incomplete.
common_mistakes: Treating it as a scalar and dropping the direction.

recall.must_convey: That the SI unit is newton per kilogram, the same as metre per second squared, and it equals g at the surface.
accept: same as metre per second squared
